Socrates: “We must always be questioning things—questioning our current knowledge and asking new questions.”

Me: “Right—getting to the truth of things, separating illusion from reality. Plato, your theory of forms recognizes the existence of abstract, eternal truths—that seem to be difficult to establish in the real world.”

Plato: “We should always seek knowledge in the outside world; we must also look toward eternal forms which contain the true essence of all things.”

Me: “Interesting. Descartes, do you think it is reasonable that perceiving a person and interacting with them in the physical world is the only way to understand a person?”

Descartes: “We need to find one fundamental truth on which we can build our entire system."

Me: “Fascinating, thanks for the clarification. And what about you, Nietzsche? You said that moral principles were ultimately subjective in nature.”

Nietzsche: “Any formation of greatness relies upon one’s self-assured pursuit of his own personal goals, not on the weak or the herd.”

Me: “Fantastic, what an engaging conversation. I feel fortunate to hear your perspectives tonight.”
